summary: Microeconomics, one metrics sequence and at least three more courses numbered 105-299 make up the 45 units, with at least 40 units in Economics, at most 5 units outside it and at most 5 thesis units of ECON 400. Microeconomics and the metrics courses need a letter grade and a B- or better. You then either submit two term papers, which your advisor checks, or take two more 200-level ECON lecture courses for a letter grade beyond the 45 units. Your advisor also checks the 3.0 GPA, that lecture courses were letter graded, and that all units were taken at Stanford.

children.name: Complete additional coursework toward the 45 unit requirement:
children.desc: Any undergraduate courses taken must be numbered 105 or higher. No seminar courses numbered 300 or above can be counted. A maximum of five credit units can be earned for a thesis (Econ 400 or comparable MA thesis or dissertation course in another department) toward the 45-unit degree requirement. Whether a course is a lecture (letter grade) is checked by hand; a 300-level course that is not a seminar is moved in by hand.
